chunks: Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from al-Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man says to his wife,
He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no expiation upon him, nor a divorce.'

key_terms.حَرَامٌ: Prohibited (specifically referring to Zihar or general prohibition in this context)
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation (penalty for breaking an oath or Zihar)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a man tells his wife she is prohibited to him?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the phrase 'You are prohibited unto me' does not automatically trigger the formal expiation (Kaffarah) of Zihar nor constitute a revocable divorce (Talaq), highlighting the precision required in marital declarations. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between specific legal formulas and general statements of prohibition, ensuring that marital status is not altered without clear intent. The context reflects the broader Islamic legal principle that words are interpreted according to their specific technical meanings within the family law framework.

en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from Safwan from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who says to his wife, ‘
